uncited: This family extends 3D Gaussian Splatting to support physically based lighting, self-occlusion, and environment reflections [4464-ref-gaussian-deferred-surfel-rendering-with-split-sum-ibl.md, 4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t_light.md, 4489-light-space-rasterization-for-t_light.md].

It solves the limitation of standard splatting, which assumes a fixed, uniform lighting environment, by introducing deferred shading pipelines for relighting [4464-ref-gaussian-deferred-surfel-rendering-with-split-sum-ibl.md] and dedicated light-space rasterization passes for self-shadowing [4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t_light.md, 4489-light-space-rasterization-for-t_light.md].

Unlike sibling methods that may use simplified shading functions or voxel-based fallbacks, these approaches provide full PBR material attributes and continuous differentiable gradients for shadows without modifying the primary camera's covariance expansion [4464-ref-gaussian-deferred-surfel-rendering-with-split-sum-ibl.md, 4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t_light.md, 4489-light-space-rasterization-for-t_light.md].

For relighting, splats must carry physical material attributes: normal, roughness, reflectance (specular strength), and albedo (diffuse color) [4464-ref-gaussian-deferred-surfel-rendering-with-split-sum-ibl.md].
These are stored in a parallel Material Buffer aligned with the Splat Buffer [4464-ref-gaussian-deferred-surfel-rendering-with-split-sum-ibl.md].
For self-shadowing, a virtual "sun camera" is constructed to simulate a directional light source [4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t_light.md, 4489-light-space-rasterization-for-t_light.md].

This camera is placed at a large distance with a narrow field of view (FOV) to minimize parallax error to below 2% [4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t_light.md, 4489-light-space-rasterization-for-t_light.md].
Both relighting (for cache locality) and shadowing (for correct front-to-back accumulation) require sorting.
Relighting uses spatial locality algorithms like Morton codes [4464-ref-gaussian-deferred-surfel-rendering-with-split-sum-ibl.md].
Shadowing sorts Gaussians by depth relative to the sun camera [4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t_light.md, 4489-light-space-rasterization-for-t_light.md].

During the light pass for shadowing, the projection covariance is not expanded by $0.3I$ and no amplitude compensation is applied, preserving the main camera pass's sampling expansion [4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t_light.md].

In shadowing calculations, sun camera framing, sorting, coverage, and threshold branches are treated as constants to prevent incorrect gradient propagation [4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t_light.md, 4489-light-space-rasterization-for-t_light.md].

The methods in this family originate from the need to extend 3D Gaussian Splatting beyond simple diffuse rendering [4464-ref-gaussian-deferred-surfel-rendering-with-split-sum-ibl.md, 4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t_light.md, 4489-light-space-rasterization-for-t_light.md].
Ref-Gaussian introduces deferred surfel rendering to handle PBR materials [4464-ref-gaussian-deferred-surfel-rendering-with-split-sum-ibl.md].

The T_light methods were developed to add self-shadowing capabilities, initially using voxel-based caches and later refined into a differentiable rasterization approach [4487-3d-gaussian-splatting-self-shadowing-t_light.md, 4489-light-space-rasterization-for-t_light.md].
